title: Accessibility to Higher Education and Inter-regional Mobility
abstract: arXiv:2611.00630v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We develop an equilibrium model of the undergraduate higher education market that incorporates interregional mobility for enrollment. An individual chooses a college to attend, seeking to maximize utility depending on the quality of education and the costs of attendance. Costs include tuition fees, the effort required to pass the entrance exam, and moving costs from one's hometown to the region where the college is located. Each college admits students whose entrance exam scores exceed a certain threshold, which we call the college's qualifying score. In our model, the qualifying score of each college is determined endogenously as the shadow price of the constraint that the number of enrolled students must not exceed capacity. We structurally estimate the model's parameters by simulating equilibrium using Japanese data. translated_title: 高等教育的可及性与跨区域流动性
translated_abstract: 我们开发了一个本科高等教育市场的均衡模型，其中纳入了入学时的跨区域流动。个人选择就读的大学，以最大化取决于教育质量和就读成本的效用。成本包括学费、通过入学考试所需的努力，以及从家乡搬到大学所在地区的迁移成本。每所大学录取入学考试成绩超过某一门槛的学生，我们将这一门槛称为该大学的录取分数线。在我们的模型中，每所大学的录取分数线是内生决定的，即作为“入学学生人数不得超过学校容量”这一约束条件的影子价格。我们利用日本数据，通过模拟均衡对模型参数进行了结构估计。基于实证结果和反事实实验，我们评估了高等教育入学机会差异所带来的福利成本。
tldr: 本文构建了一个纳入跨区域流动的本科高等教育市场均衡模型，其中大学录取分数线作为容量约束的影子价格被内生决定，利用日本数据进行结构估计，并据此评估了高等教育入学机会地区差异的福利成本。
en_tdlr: This paper develops an equilibrium model of the undergraduate higher education market with interregional mobility, in which each college's qualifying score is endogenously determined as the shadow price of its capacity constraint, and uses Japanese data to structurally estimate the model and evaluate the welfare costs of disparities in access to higher education.
